the wear rate and the friction coefficient of the porous glass-cerdamic layers produced by pulsed laser ablation are strongly affected by the type of counterbody and the sliding conditions.

the wear behavior and microstructure of the porous layers produced by laser irradiation in glass-ceramics substrates are strongly influenced by the laser processing parameters and by the counterbody material.

the porous layers produced by pulsed laser in the glass-ceramic substrate show a higher wear rate and friction coefficient than expected for dense materials, and that the material transfer from the ball to porous glass-ceramics layer occurs in the tests carried out against an AISI316 counterbody.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the wear behavior of glass-ceramic materials with a porous structure produced by laser irradiation.
the development of a porous layer by pulsed laser ablation in a glass-ceramic substrate.

the development of a new technique to produce porous layers on the surface of glass-ceramics substrates by means of pulsed laser irradiations and with the study of their wear behavior under unidirectional dry sliding conditions.

the porous layer produced by pulsed laser treatment in glass-ceramics is not an adequate tribological coating for applications where wear and friction reduction are required.
, in the case studied, the presence of the porous layer does not improve the wear performance of the glass-ceramic substrate.
the wear mechanisms are strongly influenced by the microstructure of the porous layer and the type of ball counterbody.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
porous layers produced in the glass-ceramics by pulsed laser treatment can be used as a wear resistant material for tribological applications.
the wear behavior of porous glass-ceramics is mainly governed by the microstructural characteristics of the material.
the wear rate and friction coefficient of glass-ceramics can be modified by the laser processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laser-induced porous layers can be used as sacrificial layers to protect the substrate against wear.
the porous layer produced by laser irradiation can be a promising candidate as a tribological material in applications such as bearings or gears.
the porous layer produced by pulsed laser ablation in the glass-ceramics substrate can be used for the fabrication of wear-resistant coatings.
